_meta.description: Physics-informed guardrails for the legume nitrogen carry-over credit, replacing a flat 30-50 kg/ha assumption. Bounds are derived from the structure of the INRAE STICS soil-crop model and the AzoFert nitrogen advice method: the credit scales with legume biomass actually produced, is capped by mineralisation potential, and is reduced by over-winter leaching risk on light soils under wet autumns.
_meta.source: Structure and parameter ranges consistent with INRAE STICS / AzoFert published formulations and Terres Inovia nitrogen carry-over references.
_meta.caution: These are lookup bounds for a hackathon prototype, NOT a calibrated STICS run. A production system should call STICS or AzoFert directly.

credit_model.note: The damping exponent below 1 reflects that residue N does not scale linearly with grain yield; a double-yield crop does not leave double the available N.

soil_mineralisation_factor.note: Cool, heavy or shallow soils mineralise residue N more slowly, so less of it is available to the following wheat in its uptake window.

leaching_loss_fraction.description: Fraction of residue N lost over winter, as a function of autumn-winter drainage and soil water capacity. Light soils under a wet autumn lose the most.
leaching_loss_fraction.cover_crop_note: A well-established cover crop (CIPAN) after the legume retains a large share of the residue N and is already mandatory in zones vulnerables.

following_wheat_yield_response.description: Yield gain of the following winter wheat after a grain legume versus after a cereal. Published French trial means cluster nearer +0.4 t/ha than the +0.8 t/ha sometimes quoted, and the gain SHRINKS when the legume yielded poorly or the site is drought-limited.
following_wheat_yield_response.note: Only part of this gain is nitrogen; the rest is the break-crop effect on take-all (piétin-échaudage) and grass weeds. Lentil and chickpea leave little biomass, hence the smaller gain.

wheat_n_dose_reduction.description: Mandatory deduction applied to the following wheat's nitrogen dose in the fertiliser plan, capped so the model never predicts an agronomically absurd saving.
wheat_n_dose_reduction.note: Even the best legume precedent cannot replace more than about a third of a winter wheat nitrogen budget without yield or protein penalty.
